Those two isolates are drawn in the accent color, and the card returns their ids [4, 6]." width="100%"} An isolate is a node with degree zero: no edges in or out. Isolates often signal data problems (records that failed to link, entities filtered out of every relationship) or simply members with no ties, and many analyses drop them first. On a directed graph a node is isolated only if it has neither incoming nor outgoing edges. A node with a self-loop is not isolated. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted IDs of the isolated nodes. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Nodes that never appear in an edge are isolates: ::: {#8df5b185 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in graph.isolates()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['D', 'E'] ``` ::: ::: Removing them leaves only the connected part, ready for analysis: ::: {#0ff6e3bf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} for node in graph.isolates(): graph.delete_node(node) graph.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: :::
